claim: The contractless field filter is inverted. `IsPublicReadWrite` accepts a field only when `field.IsReadOnly` is true. A public mutable field of T (e.g. `public int Counter;`) is therefore never serialized, which breaks 'contractless behaviour over public members'. A public `readonly` field is selected instead. `CreateMember` hard-codes `IsWritable: true`, so the generated Deserialize assigns to the readonly field and Project B fails to compile (CS0191). The same filter makes surrogate keys that name a mutable field report MsgPack022.

claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored, although the acceptance criteria require them to be honoured. With no surrogate, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which uses string keys by member name. It never checks T for `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` or `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]`. A T in a referenced assembly with `[MessagePackObject]` and `[Key(0)]`, `[Key(1)]` therefore gets a map formatter keyed by name instead of the array layout its attributes define. `[IgnoreMember]` members are serialized anyway.

claim: The contractless field filter is inverted. `IsPublicReadWrite` accepts an `IFieldSymbol` only when `field.IsReadOnly` is true. As a result, ordinary mutable public fields (`public int X;`) are never serialized, which breaks the documented and required 'every public read-write instance property and field'. This hits structs and DTOs from referenced assemblies that expose plain fields: they silently produce empty or partial payloads, so data is lost on round-trip.

claim: Contractless mode silently drops public get-only properties and readonly fields, and the field check in IsPublicReadWrite is inverted: it requires field.IsReadOnly, so writable public fields are excluded and only readonly fields are selected. Generated deserialization code would then assign to readonly fields, which fails compilation, or members are silently missing. This is a correctness bug rather than a security issue, but selecting the wrong members changes what data crosses the wire (fields intended to be serialized are skipped, unintended ones included). Note that MessagePackSecurity (UntrustedData) handling is unaffected because the generated body uses the standard templates.
